parts.title: IQ Scores
parts.article:
A Studies from numerous countries suggest that IQ scores have been rising fast since at least the 1950s - enough to mean that someone with an IQ classed as average at that time could be labelled as having low Intelligence today. However, psychologists disagree about what the upward trend in scores really means. Some researchers argue that people are not getting more intelligent overall, but just getting better at a particular sort of problem solving. Others say they have found echoes of rising IQ scores in 'real world' measures of intelligence. To confuse things still more, there are hints that the trend may be about to grind to a halt.

B James Flynn, a professor of political science, first showed that IQ scores were rising in the mid-1980s, and became famous after others dubbed the pattern he had observed the 'Flynn effect. In a landmark paper he made detailed comparisons across fourteen countries of trends in the results of tests that measure reasoning power. Overall, these showed a real growth in scores of up to 25 points in a generation. To find out more, Flynn went on to look at scores for each type of reasoning that IQ tests set out to measure, such as verbal, numerical and visuo-spatial. This last test category usually includes 'Raven's matrices' - sequential patterns with one piece missing. The candidate has to choose, from a set of alternatives, which shape to put in the empty space. When Flynn took a closer look at the scores, the pattern was clear. The strongest gains in almost every case were on Raven's matrices and similar tests, while verbal and arithmetical scores showed more modest rises. Since presenting his original paper, Flynn has looked at data from further countries and found the same upward trend, with the same skills responsible for most of the increase.

C Flynn feels that his eponymous effect is meaningful, but does not interpret it as evidence that people are becoming cleverer. Our grandparents were not retarded and we are not geniuses, he says. More likely we have simply developed the skills and habits of mind that make us better at solving abstract problems, and - just as importantly - we take such problems seriously. Flynn believes that demands of visuo-spatial abilities have grown because of TV, computers and cars, and also that in societies where intelligence has become something people focus on excessively abstract problem-solving skills develop faster than other skills.

D Others have different views about what might account for the increase in IQ scores. John Rust of the University of London suggests that it is not just an increase in visuo-spatial activities that is pushing up IQ scores. He believes that there are several factors, including the fact that, in more complex societies, people have to think harder to find solutions to problems they face. He also points out that if just one mind grasps a new concept, such as Einstein and the theory of relativity, it may then be easier for society in general to think in a more complex way. Others, such as experimental psychologist Robert Howard, argue that overall Intelligence really has risen, helped by better nutrition, smaller families, wider access to education and other environmental changes.

E Howard's latest research has sent him on a different line of enquiry. Controversially, he now believes that the rise in IQ scores might have peaked in industrialised countries. To support this view, he cites data from Denmark. The Danish military still summons virtually all young men before a draft board to identify who is suitable to do military service. Since 1957, all 17-year-olds there have taken exactly the same qualifying IQ tests - including ones similar to Raven's matrices. Candidates must also be able to answer verbal questions such as 'Sun is to day as Moon is to ?', and number-series questions such as '2, 3, 5, 8, ?'. Results in these tests have been carefully analysed by Thomas Teasdale, a neuropsychologist. He found that during the 1960s and '70s, scores showed gains on a scale similar to those of other countries, but by the 1990s the rate of Improvement had slowed right down to about one IQ point over the decade. Furthermore, the scores were improving only on the visuo-spatial questions; verbal and numerical performance was flattening out. Most intriguingly, however, scores from 1999 onwards show an overall downturn. One explanation might be that there is some absolute ceiling to people's abilities to perform these tasks, no matter how much the prevailing culture encourages them. However, as Teasdale points out, if such a ceiling had been reached, the test results should show scores pushing against it rather than actually falling.

F Flynn is keeping a close eye on the findings, but is not jumping to conclusions until data from other countries is available. However, he does wonder whether the conditions leading to dramatic improvements in mental ability disappear as societies become more prosperous. He points out that in human history, prosperity often led to decadence, and argues that the case of ancient Rome can be viewed as an illustration of this.
parts.questions:
Questions 14–22
Which paragraph or section contains the following information?
Write the correct letter, A-F.
NB You may use any letter more than once.

Q14 Modern technology has influenced some aspects of human intelligence.

  • A
  • B
  • C
  • D
  • E
  • F

Q15 IQ scores may not have attained their natural limit.

Q16 Improved diet has a positive effect on mental powers.

Q17 Exceptional individuals can have an impact on collective intelligence.

Q18 As societies become more sophisticated the need for problem-solving skills increases.

Q19 An account of a selection procedure involving a particular group of people.

Q20 a description of one component of a visuo-spatial test.

Q21 An overview of the different interpretations of IQ score trends.

Q22 An example of the negative effect affluence may have on IQ trends.

Questions 23–26
Complete the notes below.
Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
During the , James Flynn conducted research showing that IQ scores were increasing. Flynn then analysed specific kinds of reasoning ability separately. He found that tests called , which measured visuo-spatial skills, accounted for the biggest score increases, whereas scores in numerical and components rose less steeply. Results from research in other , which Flynn has examined more recently, are consistent with his earlier findings.

reference:
Q14

解析 原文明确指出电视、电脑和汽车（现代科技的代表）增加了人们对视觉空间能力（人类智力的一部分）的要求。

干扰 你可能会在文章里死死寻找“technology”这个词，但雅思阅读非常喜欢用具体的事物（如TV, computers）来替换题目中抽象的分类概念。

句子 Flynn believes that demands of visuo-spatial abilities have grown because of TV, computers and cars, and also that in societies where intelligence has become something people focus on excessively abstract problem-solving skills develop faster than other skills.

Q15

解析 原文通过转折说明，如果智力真的达到了“绝对天花板”，分数应该是在顶峰徘徊而不是真正下降，这暗示智力尚未达到其自然极限。

干扰 你可能会看到第33句的“absolute ceiling”就直接选了，但一定要往后看第34句的“However（然而）”，转折之后的推翻才是作者真正的结论。

句子 One explanation might be that there is some absolute ceiling to people's abilities to perform these tasks... However, as Teasdale points out, if such a ceiling had been reached, the test results should show scores pushing against it rather than actually falling.

Q16

解析 原文明确列举了“更好的营养（nutrition）”等因素，确实帮助了整体智力（mental powers）的提升。

干扰 你可能会因为不认识“nutrition（营养）”而错过答案，它在这里就是题目中“diet（饮食）”的完美同义替换。

句子 Others, such as experimental psychologist Robert Howard, argue that overall Intelligence really has risen, helped by better nutrition, smaller families, wider access to education and other environmental changes.

Q17

解析 原文用爱因斯坦（杰出个体）举例，说明只要一个大脑掌握了新概念，整个社会（集体智力）就更容易进行复杂的思考。

干扰 你可能会忽略“one mind（一个人）”和“society in general（全社会）”的对比，这刚好精准对应了题目里的“个人（individuals）”对“集体（collective）”的影响。

句子 He also points out that if just one mind grasps a new concept, such as Einstein and the theory of relativity, it may then be easier for society in general to think in a more complex way.

Q18

解析 原文明确说到，在更复杂的社会中（对应sophisticated），人们必须更加努力思考以找到面临问题的解决方案（对应problem-solving）。

干扰 你可能会把题目中的“sophisticated”只理解为“世故的”，但在雅思中它经常用来表示“复杂的、高级的”，直接替换原文的“complex”。

句子 He believes that there are several factors, including the fact that, in more complex societies, people have to think harder to find solutions to problems they face.

Q19

解析 原文以丹麦军队要求所有年轻男性（特定人群）去征兵局评估是否适合服兵役为例，完整描述了一个选拔程序。

干扰 你可能不知道“draft board（征兵局）”和评估“military service（服兵役）”就是一种典型的“selection procedure（选拔程序）”，从而不敢选。

句子 To support this view, he cites data from Denmark. The Danish military still summons virtually all young men before a draft board to identify who is suitable to do military service. Since 1957, all 17-year-olds there have taken exactly the same qualifying IQ tests...

Q20

解析 原文详细描述了视觉空间测试（瑞文推理测验）的具体操作方式：要求候选人从备选项中选出形状来填补空缺。

干扰 你可能只看到了第8句的“visuo-spatial”就想选，但必须连着往下看9-10句，那才是对测试具体“组成部分（component）”的描述。

句子 ...such as verbal, numerical and visuo-spatial. This last test category usually includes 'Raven's matrices' - sequential patterns with one piece missing. The candidate has to choose, from a set of alternatives, which shape to put in the empty space.

Q21

解析 第一段开篇就点明心理学家们对智商分数上升的含义存在分歧（disagree），随后列举了不同研究者的不同观点。

干扰 你可能会漏看段落里的“Some... Others...”结构，这正是英语中表达“不同解读（different interpretations）”最经典的概述句型。

句子 However, psychologists disagree about what the upward trend in scores really means. Some researchers argue... Others say...

Q22

解析 原文提到社会繁荣时智力改善的条件可能会消失，并用古罗马繁荣导致衰退（负面影响）作为具体例子。

干扰 你可能会不认识“prosperous（繁荣的）”是题目中“affluence（富裕）”的替换词，也不认识“decadence（堕落/衰退）”，从而错过了这个核心的“负面例子”。

句子 However, he does wonder whether the conditions leading to dramatic improvements in mental ability disappear as societies become more prosperous. He points out that in human history, prosperity often led to decadence...

Q23

解析 题目问Flynn在什么时期（During the...）研究发现智商分数上升，原文直接给出了明确的时间点“mid-1980s”。

干扰 你可能会填错格式或者漏掉年代后面的“s”，雅思填空题抄写原文时间名词时，务必保持一字不差。

句子 James Flynn, a professor of political science, first showed that IQ scores were rising in the mid-1980s...

Q24

解析 题目问“什么测试”贡献了最大的分数增长（biggest score increases），原文第12句明确指出最强劲的增长（strongest gains）发生在“Raven's matrices”测试上。

干扰 你可能会错填成前面的“visuo-spatial”，但题目中已经有“which measured visuo-spatial skills”作定语了，缺的是具体的测试名称。

句子 When Flynn took a closer look at the scores, the pattern was clear. The strongest gains in almost every case were on Raven's matrices and similar tests...

Q25

解析 题目问数字和“什么”部分的得分上升较缓（less steeply），原文明确对比说“verbal（文字的）”和“arithmetical（算术的）”分数的上升更为温和（modest）。

干扰 你可能会被原文的“arithmetical”干扰，但它就是题目中“numerical（数字的）”的同义词，紧跟在它前面的“verbal”就是你要找的并列词。

句子 ...while verbal and arithmetical scores showed more modest rises.

Q26

解析 题目问Flynn最近还研究了其他“什么（other...）”的结果，原文表明他查看了来自更远“国家（countries）”的数据并发现了相同的趋势。

干扰 你可能会想填“data”，但题目问的是“在其他什么地方的（in other...）”研究，结合原文的“from further countries”，填“countries”才符合语法要求。

句子 Since presenting his original paper, Flynn has looked at data from further countries and found the same upward trend...
